[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Python re Module: Mastering Regular Expressions"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 're' module in Python provides powerful tools for working with regular expressions. Regular expressions are sequences of characters that define a search pattern. This tutorial covers the core functions: 'search', 'match', 'findall', and 'sub'."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Importing the 're' Module"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before using the 're' module, you need to import it:"},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import re"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"re.search(): Finding a Pattern"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 're.search()' function scans through a string, looking for the first location where the regular expression pattern produces a match. It returns a match object if found, otherwise 'None'."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"pattern = r"hello"
text = "hello world"
match = re.search(pattern, text)

if match:
    print("Match found:", match.group())
else:
    print("Match not found")"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, 'r"hello"' is the regular expression pattern (raw string), and '"hello world"' is the string being searched. 'match.group()' returns the matched string."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"re.match(): Matching at the Beginning"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 're.match()' function attempts to match the pattern at the beginning of the string. If the match is not at the beginning, 're.match()' will return 'None'."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"pattern = r"hello"
text = "hello world"
match = re.match(pattern, text)

if match:
    print("Match found:", match.group())
else:
    print("Match not found")

text2 = "world hello"
match2 = re.match(pattern, text2)

if match2:
    print("Match found:", match2.group())
else:
    print("Match not found")"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the first case, 're.match()' finds 'hello' at the beginning. In the second case, it returns 'None' because 'hello' is not at the start of the string."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"re.findall(): Finding All Matches"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 're.findall()' function returns all non-overlapping matches of pattern in string, as a list of strings. The string is scanned left-to-right, and matches are returned in the order found."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"pattern = r"\d+"
text = "12 apples, 34 bananas, 56 oranges"
matches = re.findall(pattern, text)

print("Matches:", matches)"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here, 'r"\d+"' matches one or more digits. 're.findall()' returns a list of all the numbers found in the string."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"re.sub(): Substituting Matches"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 're.sub()' function replaces one or many occurrences of a pattern with a replacement string. It returns the new string after the substitutions are made."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"pattern = r"\s+"
text = "hello   world"
new_text = re.sub(pattern, ' ', text)

print("Original text:", text)
print("New text:", new_text)"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, 'r"\s+"' matches one or more whitespace characters. 're.sub()' replaces all occurrences of multiple spaces with a single space."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Regular Expression Patterns"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'.': Matches any character (except newline)."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'^': Matches the beginning of the string."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'$': Matches the end of the string."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'*': Matches 0 or more repetitions of the preceding character."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'+': Matches 1 or more repetitions of the preceding character."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'?': Matches 0 or 1 repetitions of the preceding character."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'[]': Specifies a character class (e.g., '[abc]' matches 'a', 'b', or 'c')."},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'\d': Matches a digit (0-9)."},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'\s': Matches a whitespace character (space, tab, newline)."},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"'\w': Matches a word character (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, _)."},{"order":33,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 're' module is a powerful tool for text processing in Python. Understanding 'search', 'match', 'findall', and 'sub' allows you to perform complex pattern matching and manipulation tasks efficiently. Remember to use raw strings (r"") for regular expression patterns to avoid escaping issues."}]
